recommendation: Keep this commit as-is. It fixes a semantic misapplication that could lead implementers to use qualification identifiers for user identity. Broader PractitionerRole or Security wording changes should remain with FHIR-50838 or a future work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-27164 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. It requested Administration module guidance for representing user identities, guidance not to use .telecom as the formal user identity location, and identifier comments using type='USER' on Patient, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, and Person, with SMART fhirUser context that can also reference PractitionerRole.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged source commit f0c1061b32 added the Administration module section and most resource comments, but inserted the Practitioner identifier guidance on Practitioner.qualification.identifier rather than Practitioner.identifier.
additional_context: FHIR-40405 records the related FHIR-I decision to define a USER Identifier.type code instead of a core Identifier profile. PA January 2025 minutes record the final FHIR-27164 vote and creation of Security follow-up FHIR-50838, and current secpriv-module.html now contains that later formal .identifier mapping guidance. PractitionerRole was kept as contextual evidence because the seed issue's final resource identifier comment request names Practitioner, not PractitionerRole.identifier.
reconciliation: Moved the approved user identity comment to Practitioner.identifier and removed it from Practitioner.qualification.identifier, preserving the existing Administration, Patient, Person, RelatedPerson, Practitioner.telecom, and Security module guidance.
source_changes: source/practitioner/structuredefinition-Practitioner.xml: moved the FHIR-27164 user identity comment from Practitioner.qualification.identifier to Practitioner.identifier.

related_jiras.note: Resolved - change required issue deciding to propose/use a USER Identifier.type code rather than create a core Identifier profile.
Applied Security follow-up created by the PA vote; current secpriv-module.html says formal user identity mapping belongs in .identifier and links back to Administration guidance.

evidence_items.summary: Applied/Persuasive with Modification issue requiring user identity guidance on Administration and resource identifier/telecom comments.
evidence_items.learned: This is final PA intent and establishes that Practitioner.identifier, not Practitioner.qualification.identifier, should carry the user identity guidance.

evidence_items.locator: source/fhir.ini active resource and PA ownership entries
evidence_items.summary: fhir.ini lists Practitioner, Person, Patient, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson as active resources with PA ownership for the relevant resources.
evidence_items.learned: The edited Practitioner StructureDefinition is part of the current core build rather than an out-of-scope artifact.

evidence_items.summary: Before reconciliation, Practitioner.identifier lacked the user identity comment while Practitioner.qualification.identifier had it.
evidence_items.learned: The current spec had the approved guidance on the wrong identifier element, changing implementer understanding.

evidence_items.summary: The original FHIR-27164 application commit added the Administration module guidance and inserted the Practitioner user identity comment at Practitioner.qualification.identifier.
evidence_items.learned: The remaining issue is a misapplication in the original source commit, not a later policy reversal.

evidence_items.summary: Participants discussed FHIR-27164 as guidance for linking FHIR actors to security users, preferring .identifier for user identity and treating telecom as communication.
evidence_items.learned: The community discussion supports resource-level identifier guidance and does not support qualification-level placement.

evidence_items.summary: Minutes record FHIR-27164 being approved 8-0-0 with Persuasive with Modification and creating FHIR-50838 for Security follow-up.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms the approved PA scope and explains why the separate Security work should not be folded into this commit.

evidence_items.summary: Applied Security follow-up says formal user identity mapping belongs in .identifier and current secpriv-module.html contains that guidance.
evidence_items.learned: Later Security context reinforces the identifier placement and leaves broader Security wording outside this seed fix.

evidence_items.locator: Targeted validation for FHIR-27164 Practitioner edit

evidence_items.summary: The user identity comment is on Practitioner.identifier, absent from Practitioner.qualification.identifier, and the XML/whitespace checks passed.
evidence_items.learned: The committed source change is well-formed and addresses the precise misapplication.
